Hi Elena,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the thoughtful discovery. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:

Summary of needs you mentioned:
- Observability: per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, request traces that tie to customer requests
- Reliability: fallbacks and canary windows for model rollouts
- Performance: baseline and scale tests (targeting sustained bursts up to 500 RPS for inference pipelines)
- Procurement: procurement and legal will need a short SOW and a pricing tie-out for Dedicated vs hosted.

What we’ll deliver this week:
1) Comparative one-pager vs hyperscalers and OpenAI APIs (pricing/perf/observability tradeoffs) — attached: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-one-pager.pdf
2) Ops tooling checklist tailored to your observability asks — attached: ops-tooling-checklist.xlsx
3) Proposal for three tests we recommend to validate run-time behavior (throughput, traces, dashboarding).

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Rachel (cc’d) will send a technical test plan (endpoints, payloads, regions) by tomorrow afternoon.
- We’ll schedule a 60-min console walkthrough (dashboards/traces) early next week.
- Please share the Acme observability requirements spreadsheet if you have one — I can map items to the plan.

Elena — can you confirm the right stakeholders to include for procurement and legal so we can surface cost/contract artifacts?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Hyperscalers we evaluate internally: AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI. We also benchmark OpenAI for API features. Can your one-pager cover explicit differences in observability (e.g., out-of-the-box tracing, token-level billing views, dashboards)?

2) For performance tests, we’ll need to run a mixed workload: 60% short messages (~40 tokens), 30% medium (~200 tokens), 10% long (~1200 tokens). We care about p50/p95 latency and also request-level cost attribution.

3) I’m attaching the Acme observability requirements (acme-observability-reqs.xlsx). Procurement and legal are looped in for scheduling the commercial/contract items.

Can you also confirm whether Redwood provides:
- Per-route token cost (so we can attribute cost back to product lines)
- Request tracing that surfaces model variant + batch size per request

Elena Park
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp
attachments: acme-observability-reqs.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - operational tooling follow-up & comparative tests

Perfect — thanks for the file, Elena. Quick answers and proposed concrete test plan:

Observability capabilities (short):
- Per-route token cost: yes — our Console breaks down token usage and cost by route, model, and tag (we can demo and export CSVs).
- Request tracing: yes — we capture request traces, model variant, batch size, kernel selection, and a trace id that maps to request payloads in the Console.

Proposed test suite (we recommend these three tests):
1) Functional observability demo (30 min): Console walkthrough of dashboards, trace drill-down, and CSV exports. Goal: validate visibility needs.
2) Scale/throughput test (two windows):
   - Canary: 5 minutes at 200 RPS mixed workload
   - Sustained: 30 minutes at 500 RPS mixed workload (the mix you specified: 60/30/10)
   Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, token/sec, per-route cost, batch-size distribution.
3) Failure and fallback test: induce model variant failure and validate automatic fallback to smaller variant and behavior exposed in traces/dashboards.

Rachel, Vivek — can you own the technical runbook and provide endpoints, payload generators, and a Grafana dashboard export for Acme? I’ll coordinate scheduling and a staging API key.

Attached: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-one-pager.pdf (first-pass). I’ll iterate after SE notes.

Thanks,
Marissa
attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-one-pager.pdf

Hi Elena — looping in the technical details below and attached a short runbook (ops-bench-plan.md) and a Grafana dashboard export (grafana-dashboard.json) for the demo.

Test plan highlights:
- Region: us-west-2 (we recommend running tests in your preferred region; we can mirror)
- Endpoints: /v1/generate with model variants rwd-small, rwd-medium, rwd-large (quantized variants available)
- Payload mix: 60% short (40 tokens), 30% med (200 tokens), 10% long (1200 tokens)
- Batching config: dynamic batching default; we’ll provide a fixed-batch config for the sustained run to control batch sizes
- KV cache: enabled for the long prompt paths; we’ll include a test case that validates cache hit vs miss on traces

Metrics we’ll capture and share:
- p50/p95/p99 latencies by route and model variant
- tokens/sec and tokens/call breakdowns
- batch-size histogram and kernel selection logs (helps explain latency outliers)
- per-request trace id mapping to full payloads (available in Console export)

Attachments: ops-bench-plan.md, grafana-dashboard.json

—Rachel
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
